text:
omar: FYI — starting ~07:10 UTC eu-west-1 GPU pool queues started growing for 13B-llama family. Autoscaler lagging; requests are spilling to us-west-2 and we're seeing model fallbacks. P95 token latency climbed to ~3.2s. anyone watching?

nina: I see it on the dashboard — node group eu-west1-gpu-a at 98% util, queue length ~420. Admission controller had been allowing spillover, but policy intended to limit spill to premium customers only. looks like standard tenant traffic spilled too.

maya: ouch. cross-region spill adds ~120ms RTT plus cold model load cost. prefer to fallback models locally before spilling across regions.

chris: agree with maya — fallback to smaller quantized variant first (13B -> 7B-q4) then, if still overloaded, allow region spill. cheaper and lower latency than cross-region.

lee: sketched a quick tiered policy that enforces admission control, fallback, then spill. dropping it here: 

```yaml
admission_control:
  max_queue_per_gpu: 200
  token_bucket_rate: 12000/s
  tier_overrides:
    premium:
      allow_spillover: true
      spillover_threshold: 1000
    standard:
      allow_spillover: false
      fallback_sequence:
        - model: redwood-13b
          allow_fallback_to: redwood-7b-q4
          fallback_queue_threshold: 150
        - model: redwood-13b
          allow_fallback_to: redwood-13b-q8
          fallback_queue_threshold: 300
region_routing:
  spill_priority: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1, us-west-2]
  max_cross_region_tokens_per_min: 50000

# canary settings
canary_percent: 10
```

nina: that looks good. couple notes: (1) make sure premium retains spill rights to meet paid SLA, (2) track cross-region egress cost by tenant, add a console counter.

omar: +1 on cost tracking. cross-region cold loads also mean double GPU time if the source region still keeps requests queued. add a metric `spillover_rate` and a tag for `fallback_model`.

sre-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-332 for eu-west-1 backpressure and tagged oncall.

maya: i'm going to patch the admission controller to prefer fallback when queue_length > 150 and only allow spill if fallback reached its own limit. rolling to 10% canary in eu-west-1.

chris: when you canary, set `spillover_enabled=false` for standard tier in the canary group so we can validate fallback logic in isolation.

lee: query/logging snippet for the new metric and quick check: 

```sql
# Prometheus-ish pseudo query
rate(spillover_requests_total[5m]) / rate(requests_total[5m]) * 100
# kibana filter for fallback model usage
service:inference AND labels.fallback_model:* AND region:eu-west-1
```

curl example to flip canary config: 
```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane/api/v1/regions/eu-west-1/routing" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL" -d '{"canary_percent":10, "tier_overrides":{"standard":{"allow_spillover":false}}}'
```

nina: monitoring hooks: if p95 tokens > 2.5s or spillover_rate > 5% for 5m we roll back canary. alert to #oncall and #product-impact.

omar: good. also add a cost alarm if cross-region egress > $X/day (we'll set threshold after first 6h).

maya: pushing the canary now :rocket: will post results in 10m.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: admission-controller v2.14 -> canary group eu-west-1 (10%).

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded for canary nodes (10%) — no immediate errors.

maya: initial canary metrics: queue_length down ~35% on canary nodes, fallback_model usage up 28%, spillover_rate in canary 0.8%. still watching for cost.

chris: nice. if that holds, we should promote and then write a short runbook update: "fallback-before-spill" with decision matrix for thresholds.

lee: i'll add dashboards for spillover_rate, fallback_model, cross_region_tokens, and per-tenant egress cost.

nina: reminder: update the SLA doc for premium guarantees to reflect cross-region behavior and billing.

omar: thanks all. next steps: promote if canary stays stable for 30m, add cost alert, update playbook.

maya: noted — will follow up with post-mortem blurb if anything weird shows up.
